chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who performs salat (prayer) between the graves. He said: That is not permissible unless, when he performs salat (prayer), he places between himself and the graves ten cubits in front of him, ten cubits behind him, ten cubits on his right, and ten cubits on his left; then he may perform salat (prayer) if he wishes.

key_terms.عَشَرَةَ أَذْرُعٍ: ten cubits as the required distance

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) between graves in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding performing salat (prayer) between graves. It states that such salat (prayer) is not permissible unless a specified distance is maintained from the graves on all sides, indicating care for the proper place of worship in fiqh.
